title: Countable coordinate enlargement invariant under an endomorphism
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $J$ a set and $(N_j)_{j\in J}$ a family of $R$-modules, each countably generated, meaning generated by an at most countable subset. Put $M=\bigoplus_{j\in J}N_j$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules]. For $A\subseteq J$, write $M_A$ for the coordinate submodule of families supported in $A$ (the support is the set of indices with nonzero coordinate). Let $f:M\to M$ be any $R$-linear endomorphism. For every at most countable subset $C\subseteq J$ there exists an at most countable subset $D\subseteq J$ containing $C$ such that $f(M_D)\subseteq M_D$. No countability hypothesis on $R$ or on the underlying sets of the $N_j$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 058X, theorem-kaplansky-direct-sum, proof lines 20511–20552: the countable support-closure construction, stated here for one linear endomorphism; the source applies it to complementary projections.

proof.text: For each $j\in J$, choose a generating sequence $(g_{j,n})_{n\in\mathbf N}$ of $N_j$. This is possible from the given at most countable generating subset by listing it and inserting zero in unused positions; for the zero module the constant zero sequence suffices. Write $\iota_j:N_j\to M$ for the canonical inclusion of [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules]. Thus each $x\in N_j$ is a finite sum $\sum_{n\in E}r_n g_{j,n}$, with $E\subseteq\mathbf N$ finite and $r_n\in R$. The choice is of generators, not an enumeration of all elements of $N_j$.

source.place: Tag 058X, theorem-kaplansky-direct-sum, proof: the generator matrix and finite-support enlargement, lines 20511–20552; adapted to one endomorphism.

proof.text: For each $j,n$, put $S_{j,n}=\operatorname{supp}(f(\iota_j(g_{j,n})))\subseteq J$. Each $S_{j,n}$ is finite because its defining vector belongs to the direct sum [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules]. Put $F_j=\bigcup_{n\in\mathbf N}S_{j,n}$. This set is at most countable: choose a finite listing of each $S_{j,n}$, and assign an element of $F_j$ the pair $(n,r)$ of its first occurrence (least $n$, then least position $r$ in that listing). This is an injection into $\mathbf N^2$, which is enumerated by successive finite diagonals. Empty supports contribute no entries.

source.place: Tag 058X, theorem-kaplansky-direct-sum, proof: the generator matrix and finite-support enlargement, lines 20511–20552; adapted to one endomorphism.

proof.text: Define subsets of $J$ by ordinary recursion on $\mathbf N$: $A_0=C$ and $A_{k+1}=A_k\cup\bigcup_{j\in A_k}F_j$. They are increasing and at most countable. For the countability induction, the base is the hypothesis on $C$. Given an injection $a:A_k\to\mathbf N$ and the injections $b_j:F_j\to\mathbf N$ of Step 2, an element $t\in\bigcup_{j\in A_k}F_j$ is coded by $(a(j),b_j(t))$, choosing among its possible $j$ the one with least $a(j)$. Distinct elements have distinct codes. Adjoining $A_k$ uses one additional binary label. Diagonal enumeration of pairs, and then the binary label, puts this set into $\mathbf N$. This proves the successor claim even if $A_k$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 058X, theorem-kaplansky-direct-sum, proof: the generator matrix and finite-support enlargement, lines 20511–20552; adapted to one endomorphism.

proof.text: For every $k$, $f(M_{A_k})\subseteq M_{A_{k+1}}$. Indeed, for $j\in A_k$ and $x=\sum_{n\in E}r_n g_{j,n}\in N_j$, linearity gives $f(\iota_j(x))=\sum_{n\in E}r_n f(\iota_j(g_{j,n}))$. Outside $F_j$ every coordinate of every vector on the right is zero. Hence this vector is supported in $F_j\subseteq A_{k+1}$. Every $y\in M_{A_k}$ is the finite sum $\sum_{j\in\operatorname{supp}(y)}\iota_j(y_j)$ by [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules]. Applying $f$ and the preceding calculation to each term proves that $f(y)$ is supported in $A_{k+1}$.

source.place: Tag 058X, theorem-kaplansky-direct-sum, proof: the generator matrix and finite-support enlargement, lines 20511–20552; adapted to one endomorphism.

proof.text: Set $D=\bigcup_{k\in\mathbf N}A_k$. Then $C=A_0\subseteq D$. To verify countability explicitly, choose injections $a_k:A_k\to\mathbf N$ supplied by Step 3. Send $j\in D$ to $(k,a_k(j))$, where $k$ is its least membership stage. This is injective, and enumeration of $\mathbf N^2$ by finite diagonals proves that $D$ is at most countable. These choices and the recursion are all over sets: $J$ is a set and the stage set is $\mathbf N$.

source.place: Tag 058X, theorem-kaplansky-direct-sum, proof: the generator matrix and finite-support enlargement, lines 20511–20552; adapted to one endomorphism.

proof.text: Let $y\in M_D$. If $y=0$, then $f(y)=0\in M_D$. Otherwise its support is finite by [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules]. For each index of that support choose its least membership stage in $A_k$, and let $k$ be the maximum of these finitely many natural numbers. Since the $A_k$ are increasing, $y\in M_{A_k}$. Step 4 gives $f(y)\in M_{A_{k+1}}\subseteq M_D$. This proves the required invariance. Every countability bound used only generators and finite coordinate supports; none counted the possible coefficients in $R$.
